digo: Mdanga tsongo (Mdzenga tsongo); Muoga ivu (also Mzengatsongo, Chikuro)
digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III; Pakia (2005) App. VI; Maundu & Tengnäs 2005

teaser.en: Children use the dark juice of its berries as ink, and weaver birds love to settle in its branches.

summary.en: *Mdanga tsongo* is the tassel berry, a bush shrub hung with bunches of berries that ripen from red to near black. Its fruit is eaten, its juice used by children as ink, and its leaves and roots as medicine.

about.en: *Mdanga tsongo* is a shrub or small tree with elliptic leaves that are hairy beneath. Its tiny flowers hang in drooping spikes, the 'tassels' of its English name. These become bunches of small berries that ripen unevenly, so a single bunch can show white, red and almost-black fruit at once.

where.en: It grows in bushland and on forest edges.

uses.en: The ripe berries are eaten, and children use the dark fruit juice as ink. Leaves and roots are used in traditional medicine, and the wood is made into tool handles.

culture.en: *Mdanga tsongo* means 'settling place of weaver birds', a name that pictures noisy flocks gathering in the bush.

names.en: This shrub has many Digo names. Pakia records *mdanga tsongo* (also *mdzenga tsongo*) and *muoga ivu*; ICRAF and the Mgombato dictionary give *mzengatsongo* or *mdzengatsongo*, and *chikuro*. Mgombato lists the Swahili as *mziwaziwa*, *msuaga*, *mbuanono* and *karacha*; Swahili also has *msasuzi*. In Giriama it is *mhirondo* or *msimbiji*, and in English tassel berry.

mgombato: chikuro (vi) type of plant (Antidesma venosum); mziwaziwa, msuaga, mbuanono, karacha. (See: mdzengatsongo)
mdzengatsongo (mi) type of plant (Antidesma venosum); mziwaziwa, msuaga, mbuanono, karacha. (See: chikuro)
sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
Maundu, P. & Tengnäs, B. (eds) (2005) Useful Trees and Shrubs for Kenya, ICRAF — sheet Antidesma venosum: https://apps.worldagroforestry.org/usefultrees/pdflib/Antidesma_venosum_KEN.pdf
